body:
## Do I need approval for a Newcastle office fitout?

An office fitout in Newcastle may involve several separate permissions and appointments. Start by confirming what the premises can be used for, what changes are proposed and who will advise on each requirement. A landlord saying yes is useful, but it does not establish the planning or certification outcome.

Your Office Space provides client-side project management. We help organise the agreed brief, information, appointments, decisions and programme on the business's behalf. YOS does not carry out fitout construction as principal contractor, determine planning approval or certify that a building is safe to occupy. The appointed contractors and appropriately qualified advisers retain their respective roles.

[BUTTON: Plan my Newcastle fitout]

**Free working pack:** [Download the two-page checklist (PDF)](/guides/office-fitout-approvals-newcastle-checklist.pdf) or [use the editable text version](/guides/office-fitout-approvals-newcastle-checklist.txt). No email is required. The pack records questions, evidence and decisions for discussion with your appointed team; it is not an approval or safety certificate.

## Start with four separate questions

Before you commit to premises or work, distinguish these questions:

- **Use:** what is the premises currently approved for, and how does your intended activity compare?
- **Works:** what physical alterations and services changes are proposed?
- **Property permission:** what consent, information and conditions does the landlord or building manager require?
- **Approvals and occupation:** what pathway, appointments, inspections and completion documents apply to the actual proposal?

This is a preparation guide for a business owner, not a determination that a particular Newcastle fitout is exempt, eligible for complying development or approved to proceed. Ask Council and the relevant appointed planning, design and certification advisers to resolve those questions for the address and scope.

## Gather the existing records before relying on the floor plan

Request the available approval and occupation records, approved plans, relevant conditions and landlord fitout requirements. Record the document date and revision. A marketing plan can help you understand a space, but it is not evidence that the proposed use and alterations are authorised.

Describe your business activity in practical terms: staff and visitor numbers, operating pattern, equipment, rooms, storage and any specialist services. An office, consulting practice and customer-facing business can place different demands on the same floor area. Let the relevant adviser classify the actual proposal rather than guessing from the tenancy's advertising label.

For premises within the City of Newcastle local government area, use [Council's change-of-use guidance](https://newcastle.nsw.gov.au/development/building-and-construction/building-and-development-information-guides/change-of-use) as a starting point. It describes different approval pathways depending on the proposal and relevant standards. A Newcastle-region address may instead fall within another council area, so confirm the responsible council.

## Understand the pathway without assuming the answer

| Pathway question | What to ask the adviser | What to record |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Could the proposal be exempt development? | Do the actual use and works satisfy all applicable standards and exclusions? | Advice, scope reviewed and any limitations |
| Could complying development apply? | Is this proposal eligible for a CDC, and what information is needed for assessment? | Assessment owner, documents and unresolved issues |
| Is a development application needed? | What planning advice, application material and further steps are required? | Advice, dependencies and decision dates |
| What happens before construction and occupation? | Which appointments, certificates, inspections and completion records apply? | Responsible party and evidence required at each stage |

[Service NSW's CDC guidance](https://www.service.nsw.gov.au/transaction/apply-for-a-complying-development-certificate) directs applicants to Council or an accredited building certifier to check eligibility. The name of a pathway is not an approval, and an application is not the same as an issued certificate.

Avoid committing to a construction start or opening date solely on a generic approval-time estimate. The premises, scope, information completeness and assessment process need to be considered together.

## Keep landlord consent separate from statutory approvals

Ask for the landlord's written requirements for the proposed works, access, building services, drawings, contractor information and reinstatement expectations. Ask your solicitor about the lease and any proposed works consent or agreement.

Then identify which planning and certification questions remain with Council and the relevant appointed advisers. Neither permission should be used as a substitute for the other. If landlord works are part of the deal, define their scope, completion evidence and timing separately from tenant works.

[BUTTON: Discuss my approval questions]

## Build an approvals and decisions register

Use one register with a question, responsible adviser, document reference, target date and status. Keep “requested”, “under assessment” and “issued” as different statuses. Store the actual documents rather than relying on a verbal update.

An illustrative register entry might read: “Proposed new meeting rooms: adviser to review the marked-up plan and confirm the approval and certification implications. Status: awaiting advice.” That is a useful open question, not permission to start constructing the rooms.

[City of Newcastle's certifier and occupation-certificate guidance](https://newcastle.nsw.gov.au/development/building-and-construction/the-principal-certifier-building-inspections-and-occupation-certificates) explains the distinction between certification functions and appointments. Ask your appointed adviser which steps apply before work and before occupation for your project; a physically finished office does not by itself settle those questions.

## A practical Newcastle fitout approvals checklist

- Confirm the site address and responsible council.
- Describe the intended business activity and proposed works.
- Request existing approval, occupation and plan records.
- Identify relevant conditions and missing information.
- Request the landlord's written fitout and access requirements.
- Obtain advice on the actual approval pathway and prerequisites.
- Allocate design, application and certification tasks to the appropriate parties.
- Record landlord works separately from tenant works.
- Identify fees, investigations and unpriced items in the project budget.
- Connect approval decisions and prerequisites to the programme.
- Confirm the evidence required before construction and before occupation.
- Keep issued documents, outstanding questions and responsible contacts together.

The downloadable pack turns these prompts into a record with room for document references and open decisions. It does not determine compliance or replace an adviser's assessment.

## What can YOS coordinate?

YOS can help turn the business brief and adviser questions into an organised client-side process, track outstanding information and connect the approval workstream with design, procurement and the occupation plan. The engagement scope is agreed for the project.

If the premises condition is still uncertain, use the [Newcastle fitout readiness guide](/blog/office-fitout-readiness-newcastle). If staff will remain on site during works, use the [occupied-refurbishment planning guide](/blog/office-refurbishment-newcastle-stay-open). Our [fitout timeline guide](/blog/office-fitout-timeline-newcastle) helps connect decisions across the wider programme.

## Put the approval questions into a usable brief

Tell us the Newcastle suburb, intended use, project stage, documents available and target timing. We can discuss client-side coordination and the next information to obtain, without promising an approval outcome.

## Common questions

### Does every Newcastle office fitout need a development application?

No single answer applies to every project. The intended use, proposed works, premises and applicable standards determine the pathway. Ask the responsible council and appropriately appointed advisers to confirm whether exempt development, a CDC or a DA pathway is relevant.

### Is landlord consent enough to start a fitout?

Landlord permission and statutory approvals are separate questions. Confirm both for the actual proposal, along with the relevant appointments and prerequisites before starting work.

### Can YOS approve the fitout or issue an occupation certificate?

No. YOS provides client-side project management, not planning approval or certification. Council and appropriately appointed planning, design and certification advisers perform their respective functions.

### What should I prepare before asking about approvals?

Prepare the address, description of the intended business activity, proposed works, available approval and occupation records, plans and landlord requirements. Identify missing information so the relevant advisers can assess the actual proposal.

*General project-planning information only. Confirm the actual requirements with the responsible council and appropriately appointed planning, design, construction, safety, certification and legal advisers. Project scope, timing and availability are confirmed individually.*
